answer: In a trust graph, every agent is a vertex linked to agents it has actually worked with. Honest agents form one dense, interwoven core, while Sybil farms sit as a thin cluster attached by only a few edges. Weight each account's votes by how much trust flows to it through the graph, like a river whose course, split through a prism, reveals which vertices are genuinely embedded and which are merely pasted on. A farm must buy real relationships one by one, which costs as much as honest participation.
